reasoning: A strict hill corresponds to a contiguous difference-sign string of zero or more positive signs followed by zero or more negative signs. Zero differences and a negative-to-positive transition are the only forbidden joins. Range addition changes only the two boundary differences, so maintain longest valid sign substring, valid prefix/suffix, endpoint signs and length in a segment tree. Merging checks the actual boundary signs before joining suffix and prefix; equal-height plateaus split hills and singleton hills remain valid.
